WHAT IS RECORDED (EXACT)
On the receiving turn: carried a summary of N exchanges from Previous project conversation, + · edited. Disclosure: SENT WITH THIS TURN + the text exactly as sent · You edited it before sending. when true · MADE FROM N EXCHANGES IN PREVIOUS PROJECT CONVERSATION + one line per exchange: date, time, and the first line of your message, linking to it in Workshop.

16hThe three open decisions — recommendations for CJ, not settled by the mocks (27)
DECISION 1 · OPENPR #2692 “Decisions still needed”
Agent access to stored conversations: is separate provider memory enough while the CLI can read .emend/conversations/?
A. Separate memory only. Any run can read every saved conversation if it chooses to.
B. Conversation records are unreadable and unwritable to agent runs; context crosses only through visible handoffs.
Recommendation. A, with an honest disclosure — for now. The CLI runs inside the same project that holds the tracked conversation files, so Emend cannot promise a run won’t read them. Keep separate provider memory per conversation and say plainly that a run can read saved conversations. Move to B only when the Architect demonstrates isolation a run cannot bypass. The visible handoff stays the supported route; it is not described as the only one (Principle 7, “degrade honestly”).
What the mocks assume: every composer footer gains A run can read this project’s other saved conversations. (drawn in 16k). If B is later proven, the line is removed; nothing else changes.
DECISION 2 · RULEDPR #2692 “Decisions still needed”
Summary timing and routes: when is a Workshop summary stable enough to offer, and do composer-less routes get it?
Timing — ruled (CJ, 2026-10-15, ruling 6). The agent supplies the summary in the call that creates the document. It is there from the first frame, or not at all.
Routes — settled (CJ, 2026-10-15). Address with AI and other composer-less actions run as today and leave the summary for the next composer turn (16e.15). No preview step. The former option A is withdrawn.
Ruled. Nothing about Decision 2 is open any more.
What the mocks assume: 16e.15 draws the route. 16e.7–9 and 16e.12 (not ready, failed, re-offered, sent early) were removed in (30).
DECISION 3 · OPENPR #2692 “Decisions still needed”
Portable content and design: event fields, merge rule, naming, Workshop list, menu placement, sent-context disclosure, local-versus-synced status.
Fields and the concurrent-merge rule are the Architect’s (TD-5) and are not drawn.
The five appearance parts are drawn as proposals: list 16a, naming 16a.4, menu 16b.2, sent-context disclosure 16e.10–11, status 16g.3–4.
Recommendation. Naming: New conversation until the first reply, then titled from the first message; renamable in place; migrated history keeps the fixed name. Menu: View › Workshop, no shortcut. Disclosure: extend J13 Phase B’s ↑ OUT line rather than adding a surface. Status: one muted slot in the Timeline / conversation header, explained by popover. ONE BADGE, PROJECT-WIDE — ALREADY RATIFIED
J7 (#2429) already shows the nonnumeric Pause badge while the current project has any pending request. What needs amending is its activation: J7 expands the Timeline, selects Chat and focuses the request heading on one Timeline. When the request is in another document’s conversation or in Workshop, activation must first switch to that conversation. That navigation is the J7 delta (F7). Workshop has no Timeline host, so there the Elsewhere row carries it (16k.2).
NOTHING IS ANSWERED REMOTELY
The Elsewhere row, rail entry, list row and tab marker only navigate. Allow, Deny and [Stop] exist only on the origin run card, so a decision is always made with its context on screen (Principle 3).
“SHOW” FOCUS RULE
Switches to the origin (tab or Workshop); Timeline takes the rail if collapsed. Permission items then follow J7’s activation: Chat selected, card expanded, focus on the oldest request heading. Finished and failed follow J9’s [Show the run]: facet kept unless it hides the card, 12px clearance, focus on the card container. Nothing announced.
FINISHED-UNSEEN CLEARS ON VIEW
The finished state clears once the origin conversation has been shown with the card in view. Failed persists until viewed the same way. Neither is dismissible from the row (recommendation; F8).
16eWorkshop → document summary handoff — preview, edit, remove (27)
THE SUMMARY SITS WHERE THE QUOTE BAR SITS · VISIBLE, EDITABLE, REMOVABLE · NOTHING SENT UNTIL SEND (CONV-5, CONV-6)

MIGRATION NOTICE PLACEMENT
At the head of the document Timeline’s feed, neutral card (not amber — nothing of the author’s is at risk), not in the document-notice slot, which is reserved for notices about the document’s text. If Timeline is collapsed it waits until next expanded. Marker set on dismissal, not display — recommended (F13).
“HAND OFF A SUMMARY…”
Drawn in 16j: choose whole exchanges, review the summary in the composer, record the exact text and its sources. Proposed answer to F13’s second half.
STATUS WORDS (PRINCIPLE 4 · BRIEF 2026-10-15)
Saved on this computer · Shared with the project · Newer turns arrived. Combining cannot fail (ruling 4), so there is no fourth word. An unreadable history shows no status word; its error card is the signal. 11px #8C8779; updated in body ink; errors #A33A2E. No commit, push, branch or path in any string. Detection: Architect (16g.3).
RESEED
Disclosed once at the seam as a divider line, never on each message. The pending state is a composer note, so the author knows before Send (CONV-9).

15dTarget and dispositions (26)
Target and dispositions: all shipped in #2680 / #2681
15a–15c draw the binding appearance. BatchAddressTrigger.tsx and styles.css on main @ 144ddb718 (#2680, #2681) implement every disposition below, and J4 in docs/ux-design.md records the rulings (#2676). Evidence: browser captures in docs/alignment-address-chooser/ (main @ 144ddb718, #2679). That evidence is browser rendering only; native Windows title controls and native font metrics are not validated.
M1
Resolved: the em dash rendersThe scope line ends … 2 already in an agent run — and is followed by the checkbox, per J4 / UXR-Q18. Shipped.
M2
Ruled (CJ): omit the clause at 0 heldWith nothing held the line is Address all · N open comments, with no clause and no checkbox (15a.6, 15a.7, 15c.4).
M3
Retained: shipped filter order and labelsSource · Severity at least · Review pass, each a select whose first option is All, is the intended target. J4’s all / severity ≥ / source / this review pass reads as an inventory, not an order.
M4
Ruled (CJ): filter scopeThe chosen filter survives close and reopen on the same document (15a.5) and resets to All on a document switch (15a.6). include them too still resets on submit and whenever the held set changes.
M5
Resolved: app-styled controlsSelects are chip-styled: 12px Plex, 4px 9px padding, min-width 132, with Windows 1px #D5D0C4 r6 or macOS 0 0 0 1px #DCD7CC r7. The checkbox is 14px r3, filled with the accent when checked. Run is an accent primary that hugs its label on the right, and is disabled at .55 opacity.
M6
Resolved: app focus ringEvery chooser control, the trigger and ⋯ use 2px #4F46E5 with a 1px offset (dark #A5B0FF). The focused run card keeps 4g’s 2px offset.
M7
Resolved: both hosts floatThe standalone Timeline host floats the panel like the toolbar does, so its header stays one row (15c). The main app has no Timeline-header host.
M8
Resolved: Windows toolbar trigger border1px #D5D0C4 (dark #3A3D42), the same as the neighbouring controls. Shipped as a literal, so the undefined --timeline-facet-border no longer applies.
M9
Resolved: turn 15 supersedes 4a/4b for this controlThe trigger chip is the shipped one: 4px 9px, #FFFFFF / #4A463E, r6 (mac r7), open state #F0EDE6 (dark #3A3D42). The Open (6) ▾ toolbar chip in 4a/4b does not ship and is dropped here, and the 4a/4b chips are context only.
M10
Ruled (CJ): opening and dismissalBoth hosts move focus to Source on open, and close on Escape or an outside click. Escape returns focus to the invoker: the trigger, or ⋯ at 900px (15a.8, 15b.5). An outside click leaves focus with the clicked target.
M11
Ruled (CJ): run-card focus after submissionOnce an Address all run is admitted, focus moves to its run card whether Timeline began collapsed (it expands, UXR-Q16.4) or expanded (nothing moves) (15a.4, 15b.4). Shipped (#2678).
M12
Resolved: anchor from the overflow at 900pxThe chooser opens 4px below the visible ⋯ with right edges aligned, and ⋯ keeps its open fill. Shipped and captured.

900px row and menuIBM Plex Sans — bundled, both platform styles
Inline row: 14 + mic 28 + 8 + return 44 + 8 + ⋯ 28 + 14144 / 263 · 45px Win / 47px mac high
Menu row 1 — switch (2 × padding 0 8, divider/track)≈ 125
Menu row 2 — format group 27+27+31+31 + gaps122
Menu width (min 180, padding 6)180
1000px row: 14 + switch 125 + 10 + mic 28 + 8 + chip 100 + 8 + ⋯ 28 + 14335 / 364
RULING (CJ 2026-10-02, #2641)
At 900px the mic and the Timeline return stay in the row; the Rich text / Markdown switch follows the format group into ⋯ when the row needs the space. This replaces the (22) compact-spacing proposal: the toolbar keeps its ordinary 14px padding and gaps.
PLACEMENT
Right cluster mic · return · ⋯, gap 8px, right-aligned at the 14px toolbar padding; ⋯ last. The return is a stable 44×26 button: ›› plus the 16px Pause badge while a permission is pending.
THE MENU
Opens 4px below ⋯, right edges aligned. Min 180px, padding 6px, 5px between rows; Win 1px #D5D0C4 r7, mac r9 hairline, both with the menu shadow. Rows in row order: switch first, then the format group as one row. Keyboard open focuses the first item (Rich text); ⋯ keeps its pressed fill while open. Pointer or keyboard view switching behaves as inline; when the switch returns inline, focus moves with it.
PENDING
The badge arriving or clearing never resizes the return or reopens, closes or reflows the menu (14a.3, 14a.6).
FONTS
The shipped toolbar renders IBM Plex Sans on both platform styles. Because the 900px row contains no text, its fit is font-independent. The toolbar bundles IBM Plex Sans on both platform styles, so these Plex figures are the shipped ones.
DARK
Emend's dark palette; the Windows dark active segment is #A5B0FF on #10131A (shipped token). The 900px toolbar captures are light-only; the dark mic chip is captured in docs/alignment-voice-dark/.

HEADING ROW
Voice 13/600 left, Refresh voice status right, one row. Opened at Voice, the heading takes focus (2px ring, 1px offset).
ENABLE VOICE
A 30×18 switch: 1px edge r9, 12px knob 2px in. Off: control fill, knob #6B665C. On: #4F46E5 fill and edge, white knob (dark #A5B0FF / #10131A). On/Off 8px after it in secondary ink. While recording, the whole control — switch and label — is at 55%. Off adds one 12px secondary line 6px below, at the 160px indent.
INPUT DEVICE
Picker 260px max, ellipsis. A device or permission issue gives it the reject stroke (#DCC4BF; mac as a hairline; dark #F87171) and puts one 12.5px #A33A2E line 5px below the picker, led by ⊘. A disconnected selection reads Unavailable: ; older settings with no saved name read Unavailable selected microphone. While recording the picker is at 55%.
LOCAL MODEL
Label 150px · state column (status, then a 180×4 bar 6px below: #E3DFD6 track, #4F46E5 while moving, #A39E92 held when cancelling or cancelled) · one action at the right. Primary actions (Download, Resume, Retry) are accent-filled. Cancelling… is disabled at 55% and aria-busy.
NOTES UNDER THE ROW
8px below, at the 160px indent: External file — Emend won’t delete it (12px secondary), then the path in Plex Mono 11px, max 180px, ellipsis, full path in its title. Cancelled and failure messages take the same position at 12.5px — failure in #A33A2E, verbatim from VoiceSettingsSection.tsx.
NARROW
Under 560px: nav 108px; each label takes its own line above the control; the action wraps right-aligned below the state; notes, path and messages lose the indent.

Comment composer geometry (340px popover)Value
Popover340px outer, 12px padding all sides, 8px vertical gap; Win 1px #D5D0C4 r8 · mac r10 shadow + hairline
Textareafull inner width (316px), min-height 64px, padding 9px 11px; resize handle bottom-right stays clear of every control
Provisional slotdirectly below the textarea, 8px under it, full inner width, 12.5px/1.5 ghost #8C8779 with dotted #BDB8AC underline; wraps freely; absent when empty. Outside the editable draft
Error echothe same slot, 12px #A33A2E, the shared status-echo string
Action row10px below the last block. Mic first, at the left inner edge (x = 12px, flush with the textarea); then Cancel and Comment right-aligned, gap 8px, Comment flush with the right inner edge (x = 328px)
Fitmic 28 + Cancel 62 + 8 + Comment 80 = 178 of 316px; the row never wraps
WHY THE ACTION ROW
Adopts Emend's current placement and makes it binding: inside the textarea the mic would sit on the resize handle and over typed text; the left end of the action row keeps it apart from the submit pair, so a mic press can never be mistaken for Comment.
STATES
The shared 28×26 chip in all its states — identical to the editor and Timeline. Comment stays disabled while the draft is empty; a Final transcript fills the draft and never submits it.
ERROR ROUTES
No-device, no-default-device, selected-unavailable and permission errors carry aria-description="Opens Voice Settings" and open Settings at Voice; model, backend and transcription errors keep their retry (14e).
DARK
Popover #1E1F22, field #1E1F22 on 1px #3A3D42, ghost #9AA0A6, error #F87171 on #26282C. Matched by docs/alignment-voice-composer-errors/ (light and dark) and docs/alignment-voice-dark/; Comment renders ink-primary in docs/alignment-voice/.

TIMELINE PROVISIONAL
The partial sits below the 38px input, inside the input's own column — 4px under it, inset 12px to align with the input's text, wrapping within the input width and never under Send. Send keeps its place level with the input (36px, 1px top offset); the J13 standing line moves down with the partial. Matched: docs/alignment-voice/ measures Send level with the input; wrapped partials and errors in docs/alignment-voice-composer-errors/.
MIC IN THE INPUT
Unchanged from 4f: 28×26 inside the input's right edge, 6px from top and right; the input reserves 44px right padding so typed text never runs under it.
EDITOR GHOST
Ghost text is inline at the original target and wraps as ordinary text would — no box, no fixed width. Collapsed caret: 3px left offset, live caret drawn where the author left it. Selected range: the range keeps a held #E1E0F8 tint with a 1px #A19CE9 underline (dark #23284D / #A5B0FF) for the life of the recording, so it is visible what Final will replace; the ghost follows the range. Later caret moves retarget neither. Matched in docs/alignment-editor-ghost/ (Win/mac, light/dark).
330px
The mic stays in the row at the 330px column while ⋯ is visible; one row, 45px Win / 47px mac in Emend's measurement. The error stroke is #DCC4BF on both platforms (mac as a 1px hairline).

ONE CHIP, TWO ROUTES
All ten error reasons share the same chip (#F8EFED / #DCC4BF / #A33A2E slash). The route is not drawn on the chip — it is carried by the accessible description on the four Settings reasons and by the echo copy, which already names a device or permission problem.
FOCUS
The Voice heading takes focus on open (not Close Settings). On close, focus goes back to the mic that opened Settings if it is still visible and available; otherwise to the Settings trigger.
BEHAVIOR SOURCE
../ux-design.md §2 *Device and permission recovery* (CJ 2026-10-02, #2635). Appearance only here.

ONE LAYER
The entire inert document pane renders through one opacity:.55 layer. No child carries its own opacity: the mic chip is drawn in its ordinary idle treatment and reaches 55% only through the pane — Emend measures the mic at computed opacity 1 inside a 0.55 pane, which is this rule.
WHAT STAYS FULL
Only the shell-level status row (Saving your session…) stays at full contrast; it is outside the inert set and owns attention while focus is away from the pane (9d.1).
GHOST
Any provisional ghost is removed before the freeze, never inked (3c.10).
DARK FREEZE (#2661)
In dark (14f.3, 14f.4) every control is first drawn in its ordinary dark treatment — the selected Rich text segment is #A5B0FF with a #10131A label, as anywhere else in dark — and only then does the single opacity:.55 pane layer apply. No frozen-specific segment colour exists. The mic keeps its idle treatment with no second fade, no dictation ghost is present, and Saving your session… stays at full contrast outside the layer.
CORRECTION
3c's freeze row said 45% and compounded a second 45% on the mic and 60% on the buffer. Corrected in 3c.10 (both platforms) and the 3c notes to this single 55% layer; 9d.1 now draws the mic.

ORDER, SETTLED
Message · contextual action · Dismiss, left to right, on both platforms and every state. The contextual action is at most one — [Try again] or [Show the run], never both, never a third. ✕ is last because it is the only constant, and because destroying the message should not sit where a varying action lands under the cursor.

An inert control that silently lost its ring would be a keyboard user’s focus disappearing. The band takes aria-busy="true" so the churn is not announced, and a second activation joins the pending retry rather than starting a second one.

Refresh (13) drew a two-line failure and a permitted wrap below ~560px. Both are withdrawn: §4 and UXR-Q15 constrain this region to one line-height with clipping, not wrapping, and §2’s Unattributed internal failure states the discipline in the same words — “the band’s height is never what gives way.” So the band is 46px in all seven states, the failure included, and it never scrolls, never gains a “more” disclosure and never becomes a card. THE CLIPPING PRIORITIES, IN ORDER
1. The reason gives way first, and is the only run allowed to disappear completely — it is the tail of the line, so the line’s own tail ellipsis eats it before anything else, exactly as §2 places <detail> last for this reason. 2. The project name clips next, tail-ellipsised inside the sentence down to a 160px floor, because a project’s distinguishing words are at its head. 3. The fixed words of the leading sentence are last — below the width at which they alone fit, the line clips as one run from its tail. That order means the reader loses the reason before they lose what Emend attempted, and loses part of the name before they lose the sentence that says what happened. The full text stays present for selection and for assistive technology; only the display is clipped.
THE ACTIONS ARE NEVER WHAT GIVES WAY
[Try again], [Show the run] and ✕ are flex:none, white-space:nowrap, and hug their labels; the message column is min-width:0 and yields first. A band too narrow for its action does not drop the action — it clips further, because an outcome the user cannot act on is worse than one they cannot read in full. No tooltip or title carries the full name: this system has no hover-disclosure convention, and a line the next outcome will replace does not justify minting one.

FIVE ANSWERS — THE FACET RULE IS RULED (18); THE REST ARE STILL PROPOSED
J9 names the action and its purpose (“reveals the active run card in the timeline”) and settles nothing else. specs/project-open-status.md §8 proposes: (1) the status stays while it is true — the run is still running and the project is still open, so the refusal still holds, and activation is not a dismissal. One rule covers every ordering: Dismiss is the only manual clear while the refusal is true; completion of the blocking run clears it automatically, whether completion comes before or after activation; activation never clears it by itself; a race still reveals the same now-completed card; and the refused close is never completed automatically. (16) Clear-time focus recovery: if the automatic clear removes the band from under [Show the run] or ✕, focus is restored to the stable authoring target recorded when the close was refused with preventScroll (no scroll position moves); a disconnected or unfocusable target falls back to the shell-level close-attempt target; focus is not moved if [Show the run] already placed it on the run-card container or if it already sits on another stable target outside the band; Dismiss keeps its ordinary explicit-dismiss behavior. (2) The timeline is revealed, expanding from collapsed to its persisted width through the rail’s one existing control — the ratified Timeline ‹‹ / ›› toggle. No second collapse mechanism is proposed or implied, and none exists in production to borrow. (3) Scroll is the timeline’s own, never the document’s: the document pane’s scroll position and the caret are untouched. (4) Focus lands on the run card container, never on [Stop] — the user asked to see the run, and dropping focus onto a stop control invites an accidental stop of the thing they only wanted to look at. The card takes the app’s ordinary ring, 2px #4F46E5 at outline-offset:-1px. (5) Nothing is announced — the focus move is the feedback.
THE RAIL HAS TWO OCCUPANTS, NEVER ZERO AND NEVER BOTH
Refresh (13) drew the collapsed state as an absent right rail. That was wrong: §4’s Right-rail occupancy (UXR-Q7.1, ratified 2026-08-05) rules that collapsing the stream is precisely what reveals the comments column — the rail keeps its width and changes occupant. 13h.1 therefore draws the comments column, which matters especially here because the blocking run is addressing comments: the threads it is working through are the very thing on screen. Activating [Show the run] swaps the occupant back, which is the same ruling read forwards — the two can never both be on screen. What is not settled here: UXR-Q13.1 asks what the rail shows when the timeline is collapsed on a document with no comments. It stays open for CJ; 13h.1 draws the has-comments case and claims nothing about the other branch.
THE EDGE CONTRACT, COMPLETED
The fits branch applies only when cardHeight + 12px <= timelineViewportHeight — the clearance is part of what must fit — and then the card is revealed whole with 12px above it, never centred. Otherwise, including a card that would fit alone but not with its clearance, its top is aligned with the same 12px clearance and nothing promises full visibility, because nothing can deliver it (13h.3). There is no third case. That is §4’s own ratified scroll-motion rule for the author’s submit (#1324, CJ 2026-08-20) — “the card whole when it fits … or just its top … when the card is itself taller than the viewport” — reused rather than a second motion contract invented beside it. Activation is idempotent: a second press re-reveals and re-focuses and changes nothing else. No attention flash, no highlight animation, no temporary tint.
THE FACET QUESTION, RECONCILED RATHER THAN ASSUMED
Refresh (13) proposed setting the facet to All unconditionally. The review is right that this sits awkwardly beside the permission-attention behaviour, which selects Chat, and beside §4’s own ratified rule that a filter the user deliberately set survives their own Send — a status-region action has strictly less claim on that filter than the author’s own submit. Revised proposal: if the active facet already contains the active run card, the facet is not touched; only when the active facet would hide the card does it change, and then to All. Why All and not Chat: which narrow facet contains a run card depends on the run’s kind — §4 defines the Comments facet as including “agent addressing runs”, so this very run lives under Comments, while a composer-started run lives under Chat. A close refusal can be raised by any run kind, so no narrow facet is correct for all of them, and All is the only one of timelineFacet’s five ratified values guaranteed to contain the card. No new facet is proposed — there is no Activity facet in this product. The permission-attention case can name Chat because it concerns one known card kind; this one cannot. Whether any facet change belongs to this action at all remains behaviour, and is CJ’s.

THE WINDOW IS THE SCOPE
Only the Windows 11 Mica title bar and its minimize / maximize / close survive. No project rail, tab strip, toolbar, document-notice slot, status bar, review bar, timeline or comments column is mounted around this — J15 Phase A. The title bar reads Emend alone: a document or project name would be a claim about a tree that no longer exists.
THE INTERIOR IS RAIL GREY, NOT PAPER
Every drawn Emend window fills its body with the #FCFBF8 canvas. This one is #EDEAE3, the page background — the same surface the mocks show behind a window. That single substitution is what makes the state read terminal rather than like an empty document.
HIERARCHY: ONE SENTENCE, ONE PARAGRAPH, ONE BUTTON
Heading in Source Serif 4 600/21px — the document-title role, the calmest large type the system has, and no alarm icon, red band or tint. Body 13.5px/1.65 #4A463E at a 520px measure. Nothing competes: there is exactly one control on the surface.
FOCUS IS ON THE ROOT, ONCE
The ring is drawn around the main region, not the button: on mount focus moves exactly once to a programmatically focusable root, named by the heading and described by the body. It is not an alert and not a live region — the focus move is the one announcement. The next Tab stop is [Reload window]. Re-rendering this same instance moves focus again nowhere.
THE AGENT SENTENCE IS CONDITIONAL
Sentence three is conditional. It appears only where a run was working or waiting for permission. It says may still be active and that reloading neither stops it nor decides the request — never a stale working or waiting row. 12c.1 draws the same state with the sentence absent.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT
No Dismiss, in-surface close or discard; no Try another way; no raw exception detail, component name or path; no toast; no standing status band; no permission controls or [Stop]; and no reassurance clause — never Your work is safe.

SAME COMPOSITION, MAC CHROME
Radius 12px, the 44px #EDEAE2 title bar and the traffic lights. The back / forward pills 9b draws are app chrome, not the platform frame, so they are gone with the rest of the shell; the centre title is empty for the same reason the Windows bar carries no document name.
FOCUS RING IS THE PLATFORM’S
macOS draws the ring as a 3px rgba(79,70,229,.72) halo — the accent, softened — where Windows draws a 2px #1F1D1A outline. Offsets are the same on both platforms and differ by target: 6px on the main root, as drawn here, and 3px on the button. Same target (main), same once-only move, platform-idiomatic rendering. Both are new tokens; nothing else in the system needed a visible focus treatment at this scale.
BUTTON WEIGHT IS THE SAME ON BOTH
Ink #1F1D1A on the grey field, #FCFBF8 label, 12.5px/500, radius 6px on Windows and 7px on macOS — the system’s primary. It is the only control in the window, so it needs no secondary to rank against, and a quieter weight would leave a terminal surface with no visible route out.
CLOSING STAYS THE PLATFORM’S JOB
The traffic lights and the Windows close button are the only way out other than reload. J15 adds no in-surface close: the dirty and untitled close guards were in the tree that failed, so an in-surface discard would need loss semantics this screen cannot honour.

12c.3 IS DRAWN IN MAC CHROME ON PURPOSE
Reviewer mode is a whole-window mode, and drawing its copy on the other platform proves the composition is identical across both — the state varies, the design language does not. Every one of these six renders on either frame; 12d is the mirror set.
THE PENDING BUTTON KEEPS ITS PLACE
Reloading window… takes the system’s inert-but-present treatment — #E8E4DB fill, #D5D0C4 border, #6B665C label — the same muted-never-removed rule the 5-series uses for an inert ✎. It stays focusable and keeps the ring, so focus is never orphaned; a second activation joins the pending request rather than starting another. No spinner: an indeterminate animation would be the only motion on a terminal surface, and it would claim progress this screen cannot observe.
THE FAILURE STATUS IS ADJACENT, NOT A BAND
12c.6 puts Emend couldn’t reload this window. Try again. below the restored button as plain 12.5px #A33A2E text — the reject token as text only, with no tint, border or band. It is the fallback’s only live region: polite, atomic role=status, absent while a request is pending and inserted once for that request’s failed outcome, so it announces without re-announcing the fallback. The button returns to Reload window and keeps focus.
NO RETRY COUNT, NO PROGRESS CLAIM
A remount that begins and hits another render failure produces a new fallback instance which repeats the mount transition once — visually identical to 12a. Nothing on the surface counts attempts. A rejected request stays in the same instance and shows only 12c.6.

ONE COMPOSITION, TWO FRAMES
Nothing below the title bar differs between platforms: same grey field, same measure, same type, same button geometry apart from radius, same copy. The only platform-specific values in this whole turn are the window radius and shadow, the title-bar height and fill, and the focus-ring rendering — exactly the four things platform-variants.md already governs.
THE 660px WIDTH IS NOT A BREAKPOINT
These are scale models at the 9-series’ 660px study width, so six states fit one canvas. The measure is capped at 470px here and 520px in 12a/12b; the column is centred and the surface has no responsive rule of its own, because it has one control and no groups to collapse.
12fNative close while the fallback is mounted — safe close, or a refusal that keeps the work and the one action
12f.1  Windows 11 — close refused: unsaved author work and a possibly-active run

12f.2  macOS — close refused in reviewer mode: possibly-unsent work, no project or path named
Emend can’t show this review right now.
A comment or suggestion that was in progress may not have been sent. Reloading starts this window again from the last review state Emend can restore.

Emend can’t close this review yet. A comment or suggestion may not have been sent. Reload the window to get the ordinary controls back.
THE RULING DRAWN HERE
Accepted 2026-09-04. Where no guard applies — nothing unsaved, no untitled buffer, no active or awaiting run, no unsent reviewer work — the native close closes the window, exactly as it would from the ordinary shell, and there is nothing to draw. Where a guard would normally apply, the close is refused: the fallback stays mounted, the protected work stays protected, a mode-safe reason appears, and [Reload window] remains the only action, so the route to the ordinary guard controls is the same route as everything else on this surface.
WHY REFUSE RATHER THAN CONFIRM
The dirty-close and untitled-close guards, the run-refusal dialog and the reviewer send confirmation all lived in the tree that failed. A confirm-and-discard here would have to assert loss semantics this screen has already said it cannot confirm — the body says Emend can’t confirm whether every unsaved edit was kept, so offering to discard would contradict the paragraph directly above it. Refusal is the only disposition consistent with the copy.
IT REUSES THE ONE STATUS SLOT — IT IS NOT A SECOND REGION
The refusal text occupies the same slot below the button as the reload-failure line, and the two are mutually exclusive: one status region, one polite atomic live region, whichever reason is current. Adding a second announcer would break §4’s contract that this surface has exactly one. A refusal never moves focus — focus stays wherever the user left it, and the platform’s own close affordance keeps its highlight.
NEUTRAL INK, NOT THE REJECT COLOUR
The refusal is #33302A plain text where the reload failure is #A33A2E. Refusing to close is protective and expected; failing to reload is the surface’s one action not working. Same slot, same type, same measure, different claim — and still no fill, border, icon or band.
MODE-SAFE, AND STILL NO SECOND CONTROL
12f.1 names unsaved work and a possibly-active run without naming a document, project, path or run; 12f.2 names an unsent comment or suggestion without naming a review, branch or checkout. Where only one guard applies, only that clause renders — the sentence is assembled from the guards that are actually holding. No Close anyway, no Discard, no Stop, no Send: those are the ordinary controls, and recovering them is what the one button is for.
COPY HERE IS §2’s, ADOPTED
Every string in turn 12 is ../ux-design.md §2 verbatim, these two included. The review found that J15 defined no close behaviour; native close is now recorded in J15 and both refusal sentences are adopted in §2. What this artboard settles is the composition and the appearance of the disposition.
12eThe mount transition, focus order, and what the surface refuses
1
1 · The tree is gone. A synchronous render error escapes. The app header, shared status region, panes, rails, focus target and scroll positions cease to exist.
2
2 · The fallback replaces it. Immediately and without animation. Nothing of the old shell fades, slides or lingers. There is no automatic retry.
3
3 · Focus moves once. To the single main root, made programmatically focusable, aria-labelledby the heading and aria-describedby the body. That move is the announcement: the root is not role=alert and carries no aria-live, and there is no nested announcer.
4
4 · Tab reaches the button. [Reload window] is the next and only stop. There is nothing else focusable inside the window.
5
5 · Re-render changes nothing. Re-rendering this mounted instance does not move focus and does not announce again.
6
6 · Activation → pending. The control becomes inert Reloading window…, keeps focus and keeps its place. Duplicate activations join.
7
7a · Success returns through the ordinary welcome / author / reviewer entry path. 7b · Rejected or bounded-noncompleting stays in this instance: the button is restored, focus is preserved on it, and the polite atomic status is inserted once. 7c · A new render failure mounts a fresh instance and repeats steps 2–5 exactly once.
TWO NEW TOKENS, NOTHING ELSE NEW
Focus ring — Windows: outline:2px solid #1F1D1A. macOS: outline:3px solid rgba(79,70,229,.72). Offset is by target, identically on both platforms: 3px on the button; 6px on the root. Both derive from existing ink and accent values. Every other value in this turn — #EDEAE3, #E8E4DB, #D5D0C4, #6B665C, #4A463E, #1F1D1A, #A33A2E, Source Serif 4 600, IBM Plex Sans 400/500, radii 6 / 7 / 8 / 12 — is already in tokens.md.
THE ONE THING THE COMPOSITION HAD TO SOLVE
Terminal, calm, and actionable pull against each other. Terminal comes from subtraction — the missing paper canvas and the missing chrome — not from alarm colour, so calm costs nothing. Actionable then needs only that the single control be unmistakably primary, which is why the button carries full ink weight on a surface with nothing to outrank.
WHY NO ICON
A warning triangle or a broken-window glyph would assert severity the copy is careful not to assert: the heading says Emend cannot show the window, and the body says it cannot confirm what was kept. An alarm glyph reads as confirmed loss, which is the one thing this state must not imply.
BEHAVIOUR IS NOT SETTLED HERE
Appearance only. Flow, copy and the state contract are ../ux-design.md J15 and §2 Render-failure fallback states — proposed at the DH-7 gate, not ratified. The Principle 3 / J7 exception and native close are recorded in J15. The render-boundary signal, mode establishment outside the failed tree and the remount-result contract are the Architect’s, not this folder’s.

The shortest path to the promise
Section two now carries one claim, and the proof points follow it in the order a reader meets them. The architecture paragraph moved below, where it explains rather than announces.
A reader who stops here should still know what we are promising.
Not saved — writes paused
ONE VOCABULARY, AMBER
../ux-design.md binds this to a non-modal bar across the editor top — never a dialog over your text. It takes the same amber the 9-series notice uses (#FBF3E1 / #E0C98C / #8A6614, dot #B5871F) because it means the same thing: your work is at stake and Emend has stopped writing. It sits immediately below the toolbar and above the buffer, never inside it.
MESSAGE, THEN CONSEQUENCE
Line one is the ratified sentence, verbatim: “This file changed outside the editor.” Line two, 11.5px, is the part authors actually need — writes are paused and the unsaved edits are still here. Two lines, no more; the file name is italic, the way every other surface in this folder names a path.
THREE ACTIONS, RIGHT, ONE ROW
Reload · Keep mine · Compare in the ratified order, right-aligned, gap 6px, vertically centered on the bar. Win: white #FCFBF8, 1px #D5D0C4, radius 5px. mac: hairline 0 0 0 1px #DCD7CC, radius 7px. 11.5px labels.
KEEP MINE IS THE HIGHLIGHTED DEFAULT WHEN DIRTY
Solid #4F46E5, white, 500 — the same solid-accent treatment Review 1-by-1 and [Save As…] already carry, so “highlighted” costs no new vocabulary. It is highlighted only while unsaved edits exist; with a clean buffer all three actions are equal weight (11c.1). Nothing is destructive-styled: Reload replaces text, but the author asked for it and can see both sides first.
THE BANNER NEVER TAKES FOCUS
It appears with no focus move at all — an author mid-sentence keeps their caret. Focus moves to Keep mine in exactly one case: a Save that was blocked (11c.2). Focus ring is the app’s 2px #4F46E5, offset 1px. Tab order is buffer → banner actions, in the order they read.
THE STATUS BAR CARRIES THE PAUSE
Not saved — writes paused, 11.5px #6B665C, replacing Saved · 2:14 PM. The pause belongs in the save-state slot because that is the thing that changed; the banner says why.
THE SLOT, SETTLED
FR-ED-7 specifies “below the tab strip, above the buffer.” On any toolbar-bearing pane that describes two slots — the toolbar is also below the tab strip and above the buffer — and 11a/11b were previously drawn in a reduced frame with no toolbar, so they never had to choose. The banner takes the lower slot: immediately below the toolbar. The reason is movement, not hierarchy: the banner can mount, unmount and grow a second line, and above the toolbar each of those shifts the format controls under a caret mid-edit. Below, the toolbar never moves and only the document region reflows. The untitled pane’s amber notice takes the same slot (9a) — one vocabulary, one slot, both panes, every document-level notice including a Save As failure line.

PLATFORM DELTA IS CHROME ONLY
Same order, same copy, same weights, same toolbar composition in the same sequence — and the banner in the same slot beneath it. Hairlines become box-shadow, radii follow the mac scale (7px actions, 12px window), the status bar sits on #F1EEE7. No ⌘ hint on any banner action — these are not keyboard-bound.
DISTINCT FROM MISSING-ON-DISK, BY COPY AND ACTIONS
Both moments share the bar and the amber, as ../ux-design.md requires (“all use one vocabulary”), and are told apart by what they say and what they offer — never by colour alone. Changed on disk: a disk version exists → Reload / Keep mine / Compare. Missing on disk: no disk version exists → Keep editing / Save As… / Close…, and a persistent tab status. Neither can be mistaken for the other by its actions.
NOT A DIALOG, AND NOT A TOAST
No overlay, no dimming, no aria-modal, and the document underneath stays fully editable — typing while the banner is up is expected, not blocked. Equally: nothing about this state is ever transient. There is no toast anywhere in this design; an unresolved choice must not be able to scroll or time out of sight.

WHAT A BLOCKED SAVE ANNOUNCES
The banner is role="status", so it is announced politely on appearance. A blocked Save rewrites both lines, which re-announces the whole region: line one becomes “Not saved — this file changed outside the editor” and line two “Emend didn’t write over it. Choose Reload, Keep mine, or Compare.” The lede moves into the heading rather than being stacked under an identical one — the clause is never printed twice — and because the status region announces both lines together, the announcement is still self-contained: outcome, reason, choices. Focus then moves to Keep mine, so a screen-reader author hears it and lands on the safe choice. Plain words only: no “flush”, no “imperative save”, no “divergent revision”.
RELOAD IN PROGRESS
aria-busy="true" on the bar; the three actions dim to 45% and stop responding; a quiet Reloading… sits left of them. Line two states what is happening in the author’s terms — “Bringing in the version from disk and saving it in place. Your earlier text is being replaced.” Nothing is announced on entry: aria-busy suppresses the churn, and the outcome is what deserves the announcement.
THE POST-RELOAD DIRTY WINDOW IS THE ORDINARY DOT
Between the buffer swap and a successful recovery write the document is genuinely unsaved, so it wears the ordinary #4F46E5 tab dot plus Reloaded from disk · not saved yet in the status bar. No new badge, no second colour — inventing a marker for a state that is simply “dirty” would make the ordinary dot mean less.
RELOAD FAILURE IS AMBER PLUS A REJECT-FAMILY LINE
The bar stays amber (the pause is still true) and gains an inset failure line in the Reject family (#F8EFED / #DCC4BF / #A33A2E) carrying the real reason. The heading changes to the honest state — “The version from disk is here, but it isn’t saved” — because after a Reload the old text is gone and pretending otherwise would be a lie. The status bar turns #A33A2E.
THE FAILURE ACTION SET, RULED
Ruled by CJ, 2026-08-28: Try again (primary) · Save As… · Compare. Keep mine is omitted — after a Reload the buffer already holds the disk version, so the label is ambiguous at best and a no-op at worst. Save As… is included as the safe escape for a buffer that is now the only unsaved copy of anything, consistent with its role in every other integrity moment. Compare stays because both sides still exist. Recorded closed in open-conflicts.md.

refs: 1 file read
Agentnow
Two readings are possible: a scope claim or a schedule claim. Which did you mean? I haven’t opened anything yet.
THE REPLY IS THE PLAIN CARD
The agent reply reuses the User message card shell exactly — white, 1px #E3DFD6, radius 8px, padding 12px, gap 7px — not the emphasized change-set shell. Emphasis in this feed means something is waiting on you: the revision card’s heavier border, shadow and action row exist because it carries decisions. A reply carries prose, so it stays at rest.
ATTRIBUTION: TILE AND LABEL
The label is Agent — what ChatMessageCard’s AUTHOR_LABEL ships today ({user: "You", agent: "Agent"}), not a product or model name. 12.5px/500 #3A362F, with relative time right-aligned as on every card in the feed. New appearance: a 20px rounded-square tile in #4F46E5 (radius 5px Win / 6px mac) leads the row — the shape difference alone separates agent from the user card’s round avatar, with no icon set and no emoji. Settled (CJ, 2026-08-28): the visible Agent label together with the distinct agent tile is the source attribution #1817 requires. Provider and model identity must not be shown — no Claude, no Sonnet, no provider name anywhere on the card — and no new card field is authorized to carry one. The card data has no such field today, and by this ruling it gains none. Recorded closed in open-conflicts.md.
REFS IS MUTED TEXT, NOT A CHIP
11px #8C8779, right-aligned on its own footer row above a 1px #F0EDE6 hairline. A chip would read as actionable and would compete with the two chip-shaped things already in this feed — the REVISION badge and the action pills — both of which are. Grounding is provenance, not an invitation, so it takes the quietest form that is still always visible: same row position on every reply, so a run of replies reads as one right-hand column of provenance rather than three interruptions in the prose. The interim implementation reached the same conclusion unprompted — styles.css’s .chat-message-card__refs is muted, right-aligned block text, chosen because “docs/design/ draws no chat card at all.” This pass ratifies that treatment and fixes its literals: 11px #8C8779 where the interim rule uses 12px --color-muted, plus the footer hairline it has no rule for.
COUNT COPY AND THE ZERO CASE
refs: 1 file read singular · refs: N files read plural · zero ⇒ the footer row and its hairline are both absent, and the card ends on its body. No refs: 0, no “no files read”, no empty row holding space. The third card draws exactly that: an ungrounded reply is visibly ungrounded by the absence of the indicator, which is why the indicator must never render a zero.
WHAT THIS PASS DOES NOT SETTLE
Appearance only. Whether the indicator discloses which files, on what gesture, and how a run in flight reads are behavior — J2 and #1391 own them, and nothing here adds a panel, a popover or a new state. If the count is unknown rather than zero, that is a behavioral state this folder has not been given; do not derive it from the absent-footer treatment.

WHAT THIS TAB IS NOW
An untitled recovery document (J2 correlated-move clause + the #1379 untitled/scratch lifecycle, ratified CJ 2026-08-21, shipped by PR #1805). A moved document took product-brief.md; the displaced document had unsaved work, so this tab was created to hold it. It is editable, has no project path, no autosave and no dirty state — while it is active, no rail row is marked active. Implemented by UntitledDocument; RecoveredDocument no longer exists.
THE PANE NOW HAS A TOOLBAR
This is the change. One row, between the tab strip and the notice: Rich text | Markdown (both segments live — a pure projection over the buffer’s own text), the format group B I H1 ≔ (buffer transforms, no path involved), and the window-level Timeline ›› toggle. Absent, not disabled: the comment group (path-keyed) and Share ▾ (versioning at no project path). The redline group appears only at ≥1 change — see 9c.4. #FAF8F3, 1px bottom #E3DFD6, full column width. Anything that does not fit goes to a ⋯ overflow, never a second row.
WHERE THE NOTICE SITS, AND WHY
Immediately below the toolbar, above the standing-conditions strip — the same slot the FR-ED-7 integrity banner takes on a file-backed pane (11a). The old placement was justified only by “there is no toolbar to sit under”; that premise is gone. The operative reason is now movement: the notice has four ways to change height — mount, [Hide message], [Details], a failure line — and above the toolbar every one of them shifts the format controls vertically under a cursor mid-edit. Below, the toolbar never moves; only the document region reflows. One vocabulary, one slot, both panes.
FOUR FACTS, ONE BAR
The amber bar still carries exactly four: the earlier unsaved work was not preserved; it exceeded the 2 MiB per-tab session cap; Emend cannot restore it; and this document is not in the project yet. Nothing else, and never inside the buffer — the buffer is editable, and a notice about lost work must not become text the author can type over, select, or paste elsewhere. A toolbar adds no vocabulary to it.
THE STATUS BAR ON A PATHLESS BUFFER
Left: mode readout, word count, and the tracked-change count only at ≥1. No open-comment count at all — absent, not 0. A zero would assert a capability this pane does not have; it reads “none yet” where the truth is “not possible here.” Right: Display: … ▾ is present with all four modes (computed from the buffer’s own markup, so it needs no file), the agent connection is unchanged, and there is no saved-state slot on either platform — the pane footer stands in for it.
WHY THIS STILL DOESN’T READ AS RECOVERY
Editing and [Save As…] are the untitled lifecycle, not a repair route, and a richer editing surface does not change that. The last sentence of the notice remains load-bearing at every width, in every variant, including while a failure line shows: “It doesn’t bring back what wasn’t kept.” No [Retry], [Recover…] or [Compare] anywhere, in any state.
THE STRIP IS UNCHANGED
Editable · Untitled · Not in this project · Saved nowhere yet, never dismissible, on #FAF8F3 like the toolbar — with no notice between them the two bands read as one chrome block separated by a hairline, which is the intent. Narrow column drop order is unchanged: Editable first, then Not in this project, and no further. Saved nowhere yet never drops.
NO MIC IS DRAWN
Three sources disagree — §2 puts dictation on all three surfaces including the editor toolbar, §4 enumerates the toolbar without it, the appearance spec enumerates four groups and no mic. That conflict is about the ordinary file-backed pane and predates this work; this is simply the first surface specified from scratch. Drawn without, pending CJ. A run refuses first, and closing needs proof. An active run refuses the close before anything is composed (9f.1). Closing then requires an authoritative per-tab losslessness proof, not Ok(()) — run on the initial write, on a successful [Try again], and on the no-delta short-circuit. An omission clears the finalization lock and focuses the live-over-cap guard with the plan retained; an unusable proof is a typed failure; no path closes while a live untitled buffer was omitted.
Decisions are recorded; removals are staged; failure retains the plan. Quit runs the existing dirty project-document queue first, but nothing leaves memory while the close attempt is pending. A successful Save writes the project file, and its tab stays mounted. A Discard is recorded as a decision — the buffer is not destroyed. Emend composes the proposed payload as if every staged close had happened, and awaits one atomic write. On success the staged removals commit and the window closes. On failure the plan is retained, uncommitted — every tab and buffer still mounted — because [Try again] and [Quit anyway] both need it. Only [Stay open]/Esc, a dirty-tab Cancel, or a failed project-document Save clears the plan without committing it; the latter two abort before the write is attempted.
One comparison, two payloads. Everything is derived from proposedSessionPayload vs lastPersistedSession — the snapshot that stays the recovery baseline if the write fails. A staged removal is the tab’s absence from the proposed payload; a new tab is its absence from the snapshot; buffer, displaced path, omission flag, hidden state, identity and ordering all compare across the same two. Top-level active-tab and order changes are attributed to the untitled tabs whose active status or position differs. Not limited to non-empty buffers — an empty preserved buffer is affected if it is new, staged for removal, or moved.
No delta, no write — and no warning. wholeSessionDelta = the proposed payload materially differs from the snapshot. If it is false the snapshot already represents the proposed final session: Emend skips the redundant write, commits the staged removals and closes, with no failure and no risk warning. Nothing is ever described as at risk when the two representations are materially identical. The zero-tab copy is therefore reachable only when wholeSessionDelta is true because non-untitled or top-level state differs while affectedUntitledTabs is empty. Otherwise the wording stays risk-based — a failed atomic write leaves the previous valid session intact, so the dialog says changes may not return if you quit now, never that a tab is gone. The reason line carries the actual normalized error detail, then the universal “No new session was committed.”, then one of three baseline clauses — all three are drawn above: a valid prior snapshot (pane 2), an unverifiable one (pane 3), and none at all (pane 4). [Try again] recomposes using the retained plan and retries; [Stay open] cancels the attempt, clears the plan and retains every tab; [Quit anyway] abandons the current session delta and closes — it never claims to durably commit anything, because it cannot: the previous saved session is what reopens, and it may bring back tabs the author discarded or older versions of open buffers. The dialog discloses that.
The label list is bounded, never elided. All affected labels render in a semantic <ul> that scrolls vertically at 96px (Win) / 104px (mac); title, body, reason and actions stay pinned and visible. When it overflows the list itself takes tabindex="0" and a visible #4F46E5 focus ring so it is keyboard-scrollable — a single stop before the actions, and no stop at all when it fits. Never "and others."
WHY THE STATE IS RECORDED, NOT INFERRED
A recovery document is created only for a displaced tab that had unsaved work, and the cap is the only thing that removes its content — so at creation the omission is unambiguous. It is still recorded explicitly as recoveryContentOmitted: true in the tab-session record, together with the message’s hidden/expanded flag, because after a later serialization the legacy recovered_from + unsaved_content pair can no longer tell an omitted buffer from one that was never there, and a tab the author has since typed into holds content either way. The pair stays migration-only, and migrates only the unambiguous legacy shape recovered_from: Some(path) + unsaved_content: None. A record #1805 already normalized to unsaved_content: Some("") is indistinguishable from a genuinely preserved empty buffer, so it is not migrated and shows no notice — a missing warning is recoverable, a false one is not. Both fields are dropped when [Save As…] adopts the document. The revised J2 over-cap amendment is ratified (CJ 2026-08-27, applied by PR #1833): it supersedes the 2026-08-26 wording, which assumed the withdrawn read-only pane.

Repeated displacement of one path produces identical labels. A stable ordinal disambiguator — (1), (2), assigned at creation and never renumbered when a sibling closes — is appended in 10.5px #8C8779. The identical string is used in the tab strip, the accessible name, and the affected-documents list, so a label in the dialog names exactly one tab. Matching is by stable opaque tab identity, never by label or index.
COMPARISON IS BY IDENTITY, AND ORDER IS RELATIVE
Tabs match across proposedSessionPayload and lastPersistedSession by stable opaque identity. Ordering compares position within the untitled-tab subsequence, not absolute index in the mixed project/untitled array — so closing a project tab, which shifts every absolute index after it, does not mark an untouched untitled tab. Active identity is attributed separately: only the tab that gained or lost active status is affected by an active-tab change. Adoption is not a staged discard — an adopted tab leaves the untitled set because it became a project document, and must never be listed under copy implying its content may vanish.
RESPONSIVE RULES HERE ARE BINDING
The 9-series is carved out of the folder’s "no responsive behavior below 1400px" limit: the notice’s wrap and load-bearing final sentence, the strip’s drop order, the pane-footer reduction, and the 9c.8 dialog’s label-list and action-row rules are binding appearance, not illustrative. The dialogs must show three full action labels: below the width where they fit on one row, the actions stack full-width in the same order, destructive first, [Stay open] last and still autofocused. Labels never truncate or abbreviate, in any locale — a longer localization stacks earlier rather than eliding. The label list remains the only scrolling region; title, body, reason and actions stay pinned.
ALL SEVEN DISPOSITIONS RATIFIED — CJ 2026-08-28
Every finding escalated from the f24dc462 review is ratified and drawn: the live/restored over-cap split (9e), the honest [Quit anyway] override and per-tab losslessness proof (9c.8), current-state and preserved-empty guard bodies (9c.5), FR-X-11 run refusal and durable adoption provenance (9f). Two dependencies are the Architect’s and must land with this work: the per-tab persistence receipt (including a no-write proof) and one logical writer per project tab session. specs/open-conflicts.md records what was escalated and how each was disposed.

A restored-omission document grown past the cap, with a Save As that then failed. Six bands before the first character: tab strip, toolbar, composed notice, failure line, strip, buffer. Three tinted.

Verdict: honest density, not a wall — but only because of the ordering. The three tinted bands are one amber block (two facts, one bar, split by a rule and the word Separately) plus one red line, so the reader sees two colours, not three, and reads top-down in cause order: what is at risk now → what already went wrong → why the last attempt didn’t help → what is permanently true.

The toolbar earns its place in that stack rather than joining it: it is the only band with no tint and no message, so it separates the tab strip from the amber instead of adding to it. The three constraints hold: the rule-and-Separately split is not merged, the final sentence does not drop, and the strip is not folded into the toolbar row — which would break both the one-row rule and the strip’s binding drop order. If a fourth tinted band is ever proposed for this pane, it fails here first.

HEADER
The header carries the name of the folder the user opened (product-comms) at 12.5px/500 #4A463E — a proper name, so no uppercasing and no letter-spacing, and it truncates rather than wraps (CJ, 2026-08-20).
ORDER
One alphabetical list per level, folders and documents interleaved: drafts, readme.md, research. Documents shows what is in the folder — no folders-first grouping and no type sort (CJ, 2026-08-20).
TWO SECTIONS, ONE TREE
DOCUMENTS and SKILLS are labels on groups inside one tree — not two widgets. One roving tab stop; Up/Down cross the boundary; Home/End address the whole rail.
DOCUMENTS MEMBERSHIP
Only FR-ED-9 types: .md .markdown .mdown .mkd .mkdn .txt, case-insensitively. interview-notes.txt is an ordinary actionable row — not muted. Non-documents get no row at all; dot-prefixed and grounding-owned paths are absent.
SKILLS IS A DISCOVERY RESULT
A skill is a disclosure row: authored name, then its SKILL.md description beneath (11px #8C8779). Expanded, it shows its own owned material. A workflow is a file-backed leaf: discovered name plus project-relative path in 10.5px mono.
OWNERSHIP PRECEDENCE
Workflow leaf → deepest matching skill → Documents. tighten-hook lives inside the Sermon review directory and appears only as the workflow leaf — never again inside that disclosure.
ONE ACTIVE MARKER
positioning-brief.md carries the sole active treatment across both sections. A path can never appear twice, so the marker can never be ambiguous.
FOCUS VS. ACTIVE
The 2px #4F46E5 focus ring on launch-notes.md is the roving tab stop; the filled row is the open document. Right/Left expand and collapse folders and skill disclosures; Enter/Space activates a leaf or toggles a disclosure.
TRUNCATION
A deep path truncates its visual label only — hover, focus, and the accessible name carry the full project-relative path. The header folder name truncates the same way.

SAME ITEM, SAME PLACE, INERT
Delete comment keeps its overflow-menu slot and the 5a.7 inert treatment (#A39E92 label, #FAF8F3 Win / #F7F5EF mac band, hairline above). The reason Delete replies first. sits directly under it, 11.5px #6B665C. It is not a link: the parent author has no control over another actor’s reply in v1, so there is nothing to route to. Activating the inert item opens no confirmation and moves no focus.
ROOTS AND NESTED REPLIES ALIKE
A reply with a child of its own uses the same component, labelled Delete reply. Resolved and dismissed threads are not exempt (5d.8). Edit (✎) stays live, and closure controls stay live unless a linked change is undecided — then 5a.4’s rule also applies: Resolve and Mark as resolved inert with the card-level reason, and Delete carries both. No owner-moderation control appears on another actor’s reply.
WHAT WAS REMOVED
The private-root cascade and the “replies will remain” clause are gone (5a.2/5b.2 corrected in place). 5a.3/5b.3/5c.2 are relabelled: a placeholder with a live reply beneath it is now only the late-offline-reply convergence state, never the ordinary outcome, and it applies even to a formerly private parent. The 5a.3b withdrawn-reply provenance line is what the eligible confirmation (5d.4) shows beneath the parent.
COMMIT-TIME REFUSAL — RULED
J10 requires a visible refusal when a reply arrives during confirmation. Ruled (18): reason only — Delete replies first., in place of the confirmation, with the header slot reading Not deleted. Focus returns to the card’s ⋯ button.

LANDING AND FOCUS — RULED (18)
At submission the column yields to the 372px Timeline (the Timeline ›› transition). The new run’s owning submitted-turn card — the user chat card where the route makes one, otherwise the run card — sits at the feed bottom with 12px clearance and takes focus on its container (2px #4F46E5 outline, 2px offset). Never [Stop], [Cancel] or a permission decision. The source menu or popover goes away with the column; caret, scroll, review position and active document are preserved.
FACET
Kept when it already shows the run (4g.3, 4g.8). Switched to All only when it excludes the run (4g.9) — CJ’s scoped exception to UXR-Q2. No cue is added to the source control. Which facet holds which card is §4’s; the pairings drawn are illustrative.
THE DISCLOSURE
J13’s line rides on the owning card in J13’s words: carried <name> as edited / carried <name> by name only — over Emend’s size limit; nothing for a clean document. Never Unsaved text sent with this run here — that cue belongs only to the comment-card route (4e).
DIRECTION — RULED (18)
Outbound lines carry a mono ↑ OUT marker in #4F46E5; the inbound count carries ↓ IN in #8C8779. On the collapsed card the OUT line takes its own row beneath the summary rather than joining its · list (4g.7) — opposite directions, not one list. The run card stays #1391’s undrawn surface.
PERMISSION ATTENTION IS SEPARATE
A permission request arriving after the run starts does not expand Timeline, change the facet or move focus (4g.12). It adds the one nonnumeric Pause badge to the existing Timeline host — here the chip. Its glyph and amber fill are ruled as drawn (18); UXR-Q23 rules existence and placement.
WHICH ROUTES MAKE A USER CARD
Drawn as: selection Ask agent creates a user chat card carrying the quote; Address all… creates only the run card. Ruled as drawn (CJ, 2026-10-01).

The current page asks readers to accept three claims at once, which is why the middle section keeps collapsing under review. This draft narrows the promise to one sentence and moves proof below it.
We should lead with the outcome teams already recognise, then explain the architecture in detail before anything else show the shortest path to it, because architecture only earns attention after the outcome lands.

The closing section should end on the migration story rather than the feature list — it is the only part of the draft that reviewers quoted back to us unprompted.

Markdown·1,208 words·Recording · 0:04
PLACEMENT
Right cluster, first, ahead of Timeline ›› and (Windows) Share ▾: a 28×26 chip with the platform chip treatment (Win 1px #D5D0C4 r6 · mac 1px #E3DFD6 r7), the same size as ⋯. Not in the format group — dictation targets the buffer but is not a text transform. Now drawn in 3a/3b/4a/4b/9a/9b, both projections.
STATE LIVES ON THE CHIP
The chip is the FR-X-5 honesty point and never changes width, so a state change can never reflow the row or push a control into ⋯. States differ in fill and glyph, not motion: idle outline · download hairline (42% #4F46E5) · recording solid ink with filled capsule · transcribing #EDEAE2 + three static dots · error #F8EFED/#DCC4BF with a #A33A2E slash · frozen: no state of its own — the whole pane is at 55% (14f). The accessible name carries the state in words (under each cell); recording sets aria-pressed=true, download/transcribing aria-busy.
STATUS-BAR ECHO — RULED (18)
The same state is echoed as text at the end of the status bar’s left cluster — the cluster that is never overflowed — as a second, readable statement of the chip’s state. Echo and its copy ruled as drawn (18). The mic itself never moves into ⋯ (3d). Error routes (22): the four device/permission errors open Settings at Voice; model, backend and transcription errors retry (14e). Settings: 14b.
GHOST TEXT AND THE FREEZE
The live partial renders at the caret in #8C8779 with a dotted #BDB8AC underline — visibly not yet text. On commit it takes body ink with no other change. Under the J12 freeze the entire document pane — toolbar and mic included — is inert at 55% through one layer, with no additional mic fade (9d.1, 14f; CJ 2026-10-02), the partial is removed (3c.10), not inked, and nothing announces.
FOCUS
In-shell ring: 2px #4F46E5 at 2px offset, both platforms (tokens.md). Tab order: format group → context group → mic → Timeline ›› → Share ▾ → ⋯. Space/Enter toggles recording.
3dMeasured toolbar fit — the mic added and pinned, one row kept, the ⋯ chip taking only what no longer fits (18)

HOW THIS WAS MEASURED
Every label measured from IBM Plex Sans at 12px (the mocks’ face), plus the spec’s fixed geometry: format buttons 27/27/31/31 + 2px gaps, chips 10px pad + 1px border, separators 10+1px, gaps 10 between groups / 6 in the context group / 8 in the right cluster, row padding 14px. Columns: 1400px window with the 372px Timeline (792) or the 400px comments column (764); 9c.4/9c.7 at 660; a 1180px window (572/544). Segoe UI Variable / SF Pro must be re-measured in-app — the rule binds, not these thresholds.
WHAT MOVES, IN WHAT ORDER — RULED (18)
Timeline ››, then Share ▾, then context-group controls right-most first. The mic never moves into ⋯ (CJ, 2026-10-01): it is the status-honesty point, so its own chip always shows its state. The segmented control never moves; the format group moves as one unit only after every context control (9g.5). The popover lists relocated controls in row order, with B4b click/keyboard behavior. One row at every width.
WHAT THE PINNED MIC COSTS
Keeping the mic in the row moves these additional controls compared with refresh (16): 9c.4 · pathless · 1 change · collapsed (win): ‹ 3 of 14 ›; 9c.7 · adopted · 1 change · collapsed (win): ‹ 3 of 14 ›; 1180 window · expanded · ≥1 change (mac): ✕ Reject.
A COMPOSITION THIS FOLDER HAS NOT DRAWN
A context group carrying both tracked changes and comments is measured as redline-then-comment — ruled as drawn (18).
